stages.name: Tradable pollution permits
stages.title: Tradable pollution permits
stages.sub: How cap-and-trade permits limit pollution and push firms to cut it where cheapest.

steps.q: A factory's smoke damages nearby farmers' crops. To set the 'correct' tax, the government would need to know the exact pound value of that crop damage every year, even as weather, crop prices and health effects change. Can it know this precisely?
steps.right: No, it can only estimate it roughly
steps.wrong: Yes, it can measure it exactly
steps.hint: Think about how many different, changing factors go into the true cost of pollution.

steps.q: Instead of taxing pollution, the government hands out a fixed number of permits, each allowing one tonne of pollution, and firms can buy or sell them between each other. What has it created?
steps.right: A permit that firms can trade for the right to pollute
steps.wrong: A licence that fixes each firm's own price for its output
steps.hint: Focus on what the permit actually allows the holder to do, and that it can change hands.

steps.q: A firm that finds it cheap to cut emissions has spare permits; a firm that finds it very costly to cut emissions needs more. If they can trade permits between them, what determines the price of a permit?
steps.right: Buying and selling between firms sets the price
steps.wrong: The government sets the price for each trade
steps.hint: Who is actually making the offers to buy and sell here?

steps.q: The government only ever issues 10,000 permits, each for one tonne of pollution, no matter how many firms want more. What does this guarantee about total pollution?
steps.right: Total pollution cannot rise above the amount those permits allow
steps.wrong: Total pollution will fall further each year automatically
steps.hint: Think about the fixed number of permits in existence, not about prices.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: A firm that can cut emissions cheaply sells its spare permits for profit, while a firm facing high clean-up costs buys permits instead of cutting emissions itself. Who ends up doing most of the actual pollution-cutting?
steps.right: The firms for whom cutting emissions is cheapest
steps.wrong: Whichever firms the government orders to cut emissions
steps.hint: Think about who has the financial incentive to sell rather than pollute.
